purpose: Citation access-date review for acceptance rows G4.7 and G1.11. Every entry is a report-template citation that carried no accessedOn before 28 September 2026. Each named source was retrieved now over the network (NCBI E-utilities efetch for the PubMed record; PMC or Europe PMC for full text where available; NHGRI-EBI GWAS Catalog and Ensembl REST for allele/direction confirmation; doi.org / publisher pages where needed), its PMID and title confirmed, and its support for the cited statement checked before any date was set. accessedOn records this retrieval date (2026-09-28). Sources that do not support the cited statement are left undated and flagged as content defects for the owner.
integrityRule: An access date records a real retrieval that confirmed the source supports its cited statement. No date was invented. 171 of 177 citations were dated; 6 were not, because the retrieved source either names a different source/first author than the label, cites a different variant with a different effect size and sample, or reports the opposite allele direction to the report prose.
reviewer: Claude Code citations stream, agent review (not human sign-off, not clinical approval).
rateLimits: NCBI E-utilities and Europe PMC/GWAS Catalog/Ensembl were queried one record at a time with >=0.35 s between requests (<=3 req/s, no API key), per NCBI guidance.

entries.label: Saccone et al., Hum Mol Genet 2007
entries.fetchedTitle: Novel genes identified in a high-density genome wide association study for nicotine dependence.
entries.note: PMID 17158188 is Bierut et al., Hum Mol Genet 2007 (a GWAS of nicotine dependence), not Saccone et al. as the label says. Its abstract nominates NRXN1 and CHRNB3 and does not mention CHRNA5 or rs16969968.
entries.defect: Label and PMID disagree (label names Saccone et al. 2007; the PMID is Bierut et al. 2007), and the record does not support the CHRNA5 rs16969968 statements. The owner should choose the intended source.

entries.label: Thorgeirsson et al., Nature 2008
entries.fetchedTitle: A variant associated with nicotine dependence, lung cancer and peripheral arterial disease.
entries.note: Abstract supports a common variant in the 15q24 nicotinic receptor gene cluster affecting cigarettes per day and nicotine dependence in Europeans. It does not name rs16969968 or give a per-allele cigarettes-per-day figure; full text is not in PMC and the publisher page shows only the abstract.

entries.label: Li et al., Biol Psychiatry 2011
entries.fetchedTitle: Strong association of the alcohol dehydrogenase 1B gene (ADH1B) with alcohol dependence and alcohol-induced medical diseases.
entries.note: Meta-analysis (9,638 cases, 9,517 controls): rs1229984 (Arg48His) strongly associated with alcohol dependence; allelic OR 2.06 Arg vs His, strongest in Asian groups. Supports the protective His48 (T) statement.

entries.label: Bond et al., PNAS 1998
entries.fetchedTitle: Single-nucleotide polymorphism in the human mu opioid receptor gene alters beta-endorphin binding and activity: possible implications for opiate addiction.
entries.note: The mu opioid receptor is the primary site of action for commonly used opioids; A118G is the most prevalent coding SNP and alters beta-endorphin binding.
entries.contentNote: The statement that some clinical studies link G to needing a little more opioid medicine is not supported by either cited abstract.

entries.label: Schwantes-An et al., Behav Genet 2016
entries.fetchedTitle: Association of the OPRM1 Variant rs1799971 (A118G) with Non-Specific Liability to Substance Dependence in a Collaborative de novo Meta-Analysis of European-Ancestry Cohorts.
entries.note: Collaborative meta-analysis of 25 European-ancestry datasets: G allele modest protective effect on general substance dependence (OR 0.90); individual substances similar but not significant. Full text confirms rs1799971 is Asn40Asp.

entries.label: Munafò et al., Mol Psychiatry 2007
entries.fetchedTitle: Association of the DRD2 gene Taq1A polymorphism and alcoholism: a meta-analysis of case-control studies and evidence of publication bias.
entries.note: Meta-analysis: small effect of Taq1A A1 allele on alcoholism (OR 1.21), with evidence of publication bias and between-study heterogeneity.
entries.contentNote: The brain-imaging statement (fewer available D2 receptors) is not in this abstract.

entries.label: Haughey et al., Addiction 2008
entries.fetchedTitle: Marijuana withdrawal and craving: influence of the cannabinoid receptor 1 (CNR1) and fatty acid amide hydrolase (FAAH) genes.
entries.note: 105 daily users: CNR1 rs2023239 abstinence-by-genotype interaction on withdrawal and main effect on craving; full text states C-allele carriers had greater withdrawal and craving.
entries.contentNote: The statement about reward brain regions responding differently to cannabis cues is not in this source.

entries.label: Sulem et al., Hum Mol Genet 2011
entries.fetchedTitle: Sequence variants at CYP1A1-CYP1A2 and AHR associate with coffee consumption.
entries.note: Abstract reports rs6968865-T near AHR (and rs2472297-T at CYP1A1-CYP1A2) with about 0.2 cups a day per allele, in about 11,000 coffee drinkers. It does not name rs4410790.
entries.defect: The template attributes to this source rs4410790-C, 'about one tenth of a cup per day' per copy and 'hundreds of thousands of people'. The record names a different AHR SNP, a per-allele effect of about 0.2 cups and a sample of about 11,000.

entries.label: Schumann et al., PNAS 2016
entries.fetchedTitle: KLB is associated with alcohol drinking, and its gene product β-Klotho is necessary for FGF21 regulation of alcohol preference.
entries.note: Abstract supports the >105,000-person GWAS locus at KLB (rs11940694, P = 9.2e-12) and the beta-Klotho/FGF21 alcohol-preference mouse work. It does not say which allele is linked to more drinking (the template says G); PMC full text is not downloadable.

entries.label: Tobacco and Genetics Consortium, Nat Genet 2010
entries.fetchedTitle: Genome-wide meta-analyses identify multiple loci associated with smoking behavior.
entries.note: Tobacco and Genetics Consortium (n = 74,053): rs6265[C] associated with smoking initiation, OR 1.06 per copy.

entries.label: Hillmer et al., Am J Hum Genet 2005
entries.fetchedTitle: Genetic variation in the human androgen receptor gene is the major determinant of common early-onset androgenetic alopecia.
entries.note: Abstract supports AR variation as the cardinal prerequisite for early-onset androgenetic alopecia (etiological fraction 0.46) and the maternal-line point. It does not name rs6152 or say which allele marks the higher-risk form; PMC holds the paper but not as downloadable text.
entries.contentNote: 'In one large comparison study, nearly all men with early hair loss carried it' is not in the abstract.

entries.label: Richards et al., Nat Genet 2008
entries.fetchedTitle: Male-pattern baldness susceptibility locus at 20p11.
entries.note: GWAS in 1,125 men: 20p11.22 locus, rs1160312[A] risk allele (OR 1.60 across replication; 1.79 discovery), between PAX1 and FOXA2; one man in seven with risk alleles at both 20p11.22 and AR has about sevenfold odds.
entries.contentNote: 'The strongest baldness locus outside the X chromosome' is the template's own characterisation, not a statement of this source.

entries.label: Fujimoto et al., Hum Mol Genet 2008
entries.fetchedTitle: A scan for genetic determinants of human hair morphology: EDAR is associated with Asian hair thickness.
entries.note: EDAR 1540T/C (370Val/Ala), Asian-specific; the 1540C (Ala370) allele is associated with increased hair thickness and affects NF-kappaB reporter activity; rose in frequency in East Asia. 1540C is the template's G on the forward strand (non-palindromic A/G vs T/C pair).
entries.contentNote: Straighter hair, raised signalling direction, shovel-shaped incisors and sweat-gland statements are not in either cited abstract.

entries.label: Fujimoto et al., Hum Genet 2008
entries.fetchedTitle: A replication study confirmed the EDAR gene to be a major contributor to population differentiation regarding head hair thickness in Asia.
entries.note: Replication in a Japanese sample: EDAR 1540T/C associated with hair cross-sectional area (P = 2.7e-6; combined P = 3.8e-10).

entries.label: Medland et al., Am J Hum Genet 2009
entries.fetchedTitle: Common variants in the trichohyalin gene are associated with straight hair in Europeans.
entries.note: Abstract supports TCHH variants associated with straight hair in Europeans, about 6% of variance, highest frequency in Northern Europeans. It does not name rs11803731 or its allele.

entries.label: Eiberg et al., Hum Genet 2008
entries.fetchedTitle: Blue eye color in humans may be caused by a perfectly associated founder mutation in a regulatory element located within the HERC2 gene inhibiting OCA2 expression.
entries.note: rs12913832 perfectly associated with blue versus brown eyes; the brown allele is the conserved (ancestral) one; the element reduces OCA2 promoter activity; a common founder mutation explains blue eyes. The template's ancestral A = brown matches.

entries.label: Stokowski et al., Am J Hum Genet 2007
entries.fetchedTitle: A genomewide association study of skin pigmentation in a South Asian population.
entries.note: Abstract supports SLC45A2 polymorphisms associated with skin reflectance in a South Asian population. It does not name rs16891982 (Leu374Phe) or the allele direction; PMC text not downloadable.

entries.label: Sulem et al., Nat Genet 2007
entries.fetchedTitle: Genetic determinants of hair, eye and skin pigmentation in Europeans.
entries.note: Abstract reports a 6p25.3 variant associated with freckles. Praetorius et al. 2013 (full text) states the variant Sulem 2007 reported at this locus was rs1540771-T, whose signal rs12203592 captures. So this source supports the locus, not rs12203592 itself.

entries.label: Praetorius et al., Cell 2013
entries.fetchedTitle: A polymorphism in IRF4 affects human pigmentation through a tyrosinase-dependent MITF/TFAP2A pathway.
entries.note: rs12203592-T in an IRF4 melanocyte enhancer is the strongest IRF4 signal for freckles, sun sensitivity and hair colour; the phenotype-associated allele impairs TFAP2A binding; IRF4 cooperates with MITF to activate TYR.
entries.contentNote: The earlier-grey-hair statement is not in this source.

entries.label: Yoshiura et al., Nat Genet 2006
entries.fetchedTitle: A SNP in the ABCC11 gene is the determinant of human earwax type.
entries.note: ABCC11 538G>A (rs17822931): AA dry earwax, GA and GG wet; allele A has lower excretory activity; A is most frequent in Chinese and Koreans. A on the gene strand is the template's T.
entries.contentNote: The underarm-odour statements (odour chemicals, deodorant) are not in this source and no other citation on the report carries them.

entries.label: Valverde et al., Nat Genet 1995
entries.fetchedTitle: Variants of the melanocyte-stimulating hormone receptor gene are associated with red hair and fair skin in humans.
entries.note: Abstract supports MC1R sequence variants in over 80% of people with red hair or fair skin that tans poorly. It does not name R151C (rs1805007); full text not retrievable.

entries.label: Sulem et al., Nat Genet 2007
entries.fetchedTitle: Genetic determinants of hair, eye and skin pigmentation in Europeans.
entries.note: Abstract says the sixth region encompasses previously described MC1R variants; it does not name R151C.

entries.label: Sulem et al., Nat Genet 2007
entries.fetchedTitle: Genetic determinants of hair, eye and skin pigmentation in Europeans.
entries.note: Abstract: a variant near KITLG is associated with hair colour. Guenther et al. 2014 (full text) attributes the rs12821256 blond association in Iceland and the Netherlands to this study.

entries.label: Guenther et al., Nat Genet 2014
entries.fetchedTitle: A molecular basis for classic blond hair color in Europeans.
entries.note: rs12821256 lies in a KITLG enhancer over 350 kb upstream, is associated with blond hair in northern Europeans, alters a LEF1 site, and the blond allele reduces enhancer activity (22% in the hair-follicle enhancer assay).

entries.label: Monsuur et al., PLoS ONE 2008
entries.fetchedTitle: Effective detection of human leukocyte antigen risk alleles in celiac disease using tag single nucleotide polymorphisms.
entries.note: rs2187668 is the DQ2.5 tag SNP, T the positive predicting allele (CEU frequency 0.09), sensitivity 1.000 and specificity 0.999; six tag SNPs predict the risk types carried by over 95% of patients.
entries.contentNote: 'Roughly a quarter of many populations carry DQ2.5, about 1% develop celiac disease' is not in this source.

entries.label: Erlich et al., Diabetes 2008
entries.fetchedTitle: HLA DR-DQ haplotypes and genotypes and type 1 diabetes risk: analysis of the type 1 diabetes genetics consortium families.
entries.note: HLA DRB1/DQB1 alleles are the major determinants; DRB1*0301-DQA1*0501-DQB1*0201 (DR3-DQ2, OR 3.64) and DR4-DQ8 haplotypes (ORs up to 11.37) are the most susceptible; the trans-complementing DQA1*0501/DQB1*0302 heterodimer (the DR3/DR4 context) confers very high risk.

entries.label: Monsuur et al., PLoS ONE 2008
entries.fetchedTitle: Effective detection of human leukocyte antigen risk alleles in celiac disease using tag single nucleotide polymorphisms.
entries.note: Table 3: rs2187668 T predicts DQ2.5 (DR3); rs7454108 tags DQ8 (DR4), predicting allele G on the paper's strand, which is the template's forward C (non-palindromic T/C vs A/G pair).

entries.label: Begovich et al., Am J Hum Genet 2004
entries.fetchedTitle: A missense single-nucleotide polymorphism in a gene encoding a protein tyrosine phosphatase (PTPN22) is associated with rheumatoid arthritis.
entries.note: Abstract supports RA association with the minor allele of a missense PTPN22 SNP (risk allele about 17% of white controls, 28% of RA) that disrupts the P1 motif, also implicated in type 1 diabetes. It does not name R620W or rs2476601.
entries.contentNote: 'Seropositive' and 'several times the average odds' for AA are not in the abstract.

entries.label: Hafler et al. (IMSGC), N Engl J Med 2007
entries.fetchedTitle: Risk alleles for multiple sclerosis identified by a genomewide study.
entries.note: Abstract supports multiple SNPs in the HLA-DRA locus associated with MS (P = 8.94e-81), plus IL2RA and IL7RA. It does not name HLA-DRB1*15:01 or rs3135388; full text not retrievable.

entries.label: Hugot et al., Nature 2001
entries.fetchedTitle: Association of NOD2 leucine-rich repeat variants with susceptibility to Crohn's disease.
entries.note: Abstract supports three independent NOD2 associations with Crohn's disease (a frameshift and two missense variants in or near the leucine-rich repeat domain). It does not name R702W or G908R; full text not retrievable.

entries.label: Ogura et al., Nature 2001
entries.fetchedTitle: A frameshift mutation in NOD2 associated with susceptibility to Crohn's disease.
entries.note: The NOD2 frameshift 3020insC is associated with Crohn's disease; wild-type NOD2 makes NF-kB responsive to bacterial lipopolysaccharide. Supports the report's frameshift mention and NOD2 as a sensor of bacterial components.

entries.label: Nair et al., Am J Hum Genet 2006
entries.fetchedTitle: Sequence and haplotype analysis supports HLA-C as the psoriasis susceptibility 1 gene.
entries.note: HLA-Cw6 is the PSORS1 risk allele conferring susceptibility to early-onset psoriasis.
entries.contentNote: 'About two-thirds of C*06:02 carriers never develop psoriasis' is not in either cited source.

entries.label: Strange et al., Nat Genet 2010
entries.fetchedTitle: A genome-wide association study identifies new psoriasis susceptibility loci and an interaction between HLA-C and ERAP1.
entries.note: rs10484554 is the top MHC SNP (OR 4.66) and the HLA-C index SNP; r2 = 0.7 with Cw*0602 genotype in a typed subset.

entries.label: Remmers et al., N Engl J Med 2007
entries.fetchedTitle: STAT4 and the risk of rheumatoid arthritis and systemic lupus erythematosus.
entries.note: STAT4 rs7574865 risk (minor) allele: OR 1.32 for RA and 1.55 for SLE per chromosome; homozygosity more than doubled lupus risk and raised RA risk 60%. The template's T is the minor risk allele.

entries.label: Evans et al., Nat Genet 2011
entries.fetchedTitle: Interaction between ERAP1 and HLA-B27 in ankylosing spondylitis implicates peptide handling in the mechanism for HLA-B27 in disease susceptibility.
entries.note: rs4349859 tags HLA-B27 with 98% sensitivity and 99% specificity in Europeans; tags B*2702, B*2705 and B*2708 but not African B*2703 or the Asian subtypes other than B*2705.

entries.label: McGucken et al., Pathology 2020
entries.fetchedTitle: High accuracy of HLA-B*27 genotyping by allele-specific real-time polymerase chain reaction in a heterogeneous population compared to flow cytometry and single nucleotide polymorphism detection assays.
entries.note: In a heterogeneous New South Wales population the rs4349859 SNP assay had 78.6% sensitivity and 98.7% specificity; allele-specific HLA-B*27 typing was more accurate.
entries.defect: Citation label names the wrong first author (McGucken); PMID 31902620 is Jang et al., Pathology 2020.

entries.label: Ueda et al., Nature 2003
entries.fetchedTitle: Association of the T-cell regulatory gene CTLA4 with susceptibility to autoimmune disease.
entries.note: Abstract supports a non-coding 3' CTLA4 region associated with Graves' disease, autoimmune hypothyroidism and type 1 diabetes, the common allele correlating with lower soluble-CTLA4 mRNA. It does not name CT60/rs3087243 or the G allele; full text not retrievable.

entries.label: Duerr et al., Science 2006
entries.fetchedTitle: A genome-wide association study identifies IL23R as an inflammatory bowel disease gene.
entries.note: rs11209026 (c.1142G>A, p.Arg381Gln) confers strong protection against Crohn's disease; IL23R associations replicated in Crohn's and ulcerative colitis cohorts.
entries.contentNote: 'Weakens this signal' and the psoriasis statement are not in this abstract.

entries.label: Bufe et al., Curr Biol 2005
entries.fetchedTitle: The molecular basis of individual differences in phenylthiocarbamide and propylthiouracil bitterness perception.
entries.note: TAS2R38 haplotypes code functionally distinct receptors whose in vitro responses correlate with people's PTC and PROP bitterness sensitivity.

entries.label: Markt et al., BMJ 2016
entries.fetchedTitle: Sniffing out significant "Pee values": genome wide association study of asparagus anosmia.
entries.note: GWAS of 6,909 people: asparagus anosmia associated with a 1q44 region of OR2 olfactory receptor genes, defined by a self-report prompt; rs4481887 (near OR2M7) replicated at P = 1.41e-43.

entries.label: Wang et al., Sci Rep 2019
entries.fetchedTitle: A genome-wide association study on photic sneeze reflex in the Chinese population.
entries.note: Replicates rs10427255 at 2q22.3 in 3,417 Chinese participants, but states that each copy of the minor allele T raised the odds (OR 1.68). Eriksson et al. 2010 Table 10 (the source of the report's registered genotype texts) shows C carriers reported the reflex more often.
entries.defect: Allele direction conflict: Wang 2019 reports T as the risk allele in a Chinese sample; the report's genotype texts (from Eriksson 2010) say C copies are linked to more reports. This source should not stand behind the current genotype texts until the conflict is explained (allele coding or population difference).

entries.label: Adhikari et al., Nat Commun 2015
entries.fetchedTitle: A genome-wide association study identifies multiple loci for variation in human ear morphology.
entries.note: In over 5,000 Latin Americans, rs3827760 (EDAR p.Val370Ala) gave the strongest association with four ear traits including lobe size and attachment; the allele is common in East Asians and nearly absent in Europeans and Africans.

entries.label: Shaffer et al., Am J Hum Genet 2017
entries.fetchedTitle: Multiethnic GWAS Reveals Polygenic Architecture of Earlobe Attachment.
entries.note: Multiethnic GWAS of 74,660 people found 49 loci; EDAR lead SNP rs3827760 with the G allele coded positive for attachment (Latin American beta 0.062, Chinese 0.129; 23andMe OR 1.49); G frequency under 1% in Europeans and over 90% in Han Chinese.

entries.label: Smit et al., Front Neurosci 2022
entries.fetchedTitle: A genome-wide association study of a rage-related misophonia symptom and the genetic link with audiological traits, psychiatric disorders, and personality.
entries.note: Supports the 23andMe single-item rage-at-eating-sounds GWAS and rs2937573 (P = 2.58e-43) intronic to TENM2 on build 38. The full text does not state which allele raises the odds; the report's genotype texts say G.

entries.label: Yang et al., Am J Hum Genet 2003
entries.fetchedTitle: ACTN3 genotype is associated with human elite athletic performance.
entries.note: R577X homozygosity leaves alpha-actinin-3 absent in 18% of healthy white people without disease (compensated by alpha-actinin-2); elite sprint athletes have significantly higher 577R frequencies.
entries.contentNote: 'TT was rare among Olympic sprinters' and 'endurance athletes had it at least as often' are not stated in the abstract.

entries.label: North et al., Nat Genet 1999
entries.fetchedTitle: A common nonsense mutation results in alpha-actinin-3 deficiency in the general population.
entries.scope: publisher preview via doi.org (no PubMed abstract)
entries.note: Nature Genetics preview text: homozygosity for the R577X stop codon was found in 46 of 48 alpha-actinin-3-negative biopsies; hereditary deficiency is common and may not be associated with an abnormal neuromuscular phenotype; about 16% of the world population predicted deficient.

entries.label: Keller et al., Nature 2007
entries.fetchedTitle: Genetic variation in a human odorant receptor alters odour perception.
entries.note: OR7D4 is selectively activated by androstenone; the common WM variant (R88W, T133M) severely impairs function; RT/WM and WM/WM people were less sensitive to androstenone and found it less unpleasant than RT/RT.

entries.label: Fushan et al., Curr Biol 2009
entries.fetchedTitle: Allelic polymorphism within the TAS1R3 promoter is associated with human taste sensitivity to sucrose.
entries.note: rs307355 and rs35744813 (C/T) upstream of TAS1R3 correlate with sucrose sensitivity and explain 16% of variability; the T allele of each lowers promoter activity; T alleles are least frequent in Europeans.

entries.label: Egan et al., Cell 2003
entries.fetchedTitle: The BDNF val66met polymorphism affects activity-dependent secretion of BDNF and human memory and hippocampal function.
entries.note: BDNF val66met: the met allele was associated with poorer episodic memory, abnormal hippocampal activation and lower hippocampal NAA; met-BDNF showed lower activity-dependent secretion.

entries.label: Papassotiropoulos et al., Science 2006
entries.fetchedTitle: Common Kibra alleles are associated with human memory performance.
entries.note: Abstract supports a genome-wide screen finding the KIBRA locus associated with memory performance in three cohorts. It does not name rs17070145 or say that T carriers recalled more.

entries.label: Egan et al., PNAS 2001
entries.fetchedTitle: Effect of COMT Val108/158 Met genotype on frontal lobe function and risk for schizophrenia.
entries.note: COMT Val108/158Met accounts for a 4-fold variation in enzyme activity; low-activity Met allele load predicted better Wisconsin Card Sorting performance and more efficient prefrontal fMRI response.
entries.contentNote: The statements about Val carriers under sudden stress and Met carriers' stress or pain response are not in this source.

entries.label: Ferreira et al., Nat Genet 2008
entries.fetchedTitle: Collaborative genome-wide association analysis supports a role for ANK3 and CACNA1C in bipolar disorder.
entries.note: Collaborative GWAS (4,387 cases, 6,209 controls) supports CACNA1C rs1006737 in bipolar disorder (combined P = 7.0e-8); allele A carried the risk (OR 1.21 in the ED-DUB-STEP2 sample).
entries.contentNote: The brain-imaging statements are not in this source.

entries.label: Katzenberg et al., Sleep 1998
entries.fetchedTitle: A CLOCK polymorphism associated with human diurnal preference.
entries.note: In 410 adults, carriers of CLOCK 3111C had lower Horne-Ostberg scores (shifted toward eveningness) and a 10- to 44-minute delay in preferred activity or sleep timing.

entries.label: Hida et al., Sci Rep 2014
entries.fetchedTitle: Screening of clock gene polymorphisms demonstrates association of a PER3 polymorphism with morningness-eveningness preference and circadian rhythm sleep disorder.
entries.note: Supports the minor G allele of rs228697 being more frequent in evening types (OR 2.483). But the paper found the G allele enriched in free-running type (FRT) individuals, and states that DSPT (delayed sleep phase type) was not associated with any PER3 polymorphism. It names the residue change P864A, not Pro415Ala.
entries.defect: The report says the G allele was more frequent 'in people with delayed sleep-wake phase disorder'; the cited paper found no DSPT association and reported free-running type instead. The report also names the change Pro415Ala where the paper says P864A.

entries.label: Dubal et al., Cell Rep 2014
entries.fetchedTitle: Life extension factor klotho enhances cognition.
entries.note: KL-VS heterozygosity is associated with enhanced cognition in three cohorts and with higher serum klotho; heterozygote frequency 26% (typical 20-25%).
entries.contentNote: The study excluded KL-VS homozygotes, so the GG text's 'did not show the cognitive advantage in the reported studies' is not supported by this source.

entries.label: Rodrigues et al., PNAS 2009
entries.fetchedTitle: Oxytocin receptor genetic variation relates to empathy and stress reactivity in humans.
entries.note: Compared with rs53576 GG, A carriers showed lower empathy (Reading the Mind in the Eyes test and a dispositional scale) and higher physiological and dispositional stress reactivity.

entries.label: Parasuraman et al., Psychol Sci 2005
entries.fetchedTitle: Beyond heritability: neurotransmitter genes differentially modulate visuospatial attention and working memory.
entries.note: Abstract supports a T-to-C CHRNA4 polymorphism whose C-allele dose increased valid-cue benefits and reduced invalid-cue costs in 89 adults. It does not name rs1044396 or C1545T; full text not retrievable.

entries.label: Tomlinson et al., Nat Genet 2007
entries.fetchedTitle: A genome-wide association scan of tag SNPs identifies a susceptibility variant for colorectal cancer at 8q24.21.
entries.note: rs6983267 at 8q24.21 associated with colorectal cancer (P = 1.27e-14; heterozygote OR 1.27, homozygote OR 1.47); GWAS Catalog GCST000053 records the risk allele as rs6983267-G.

entries.label: Yeager et al., Nat Genet 2007
entries.fetchedTitle: Genome-wide association study of prostate cancer identifies a second risk locus at 8q24.
entries.note: rs6983267 at 8q24 associated with prostate cancer (P = 9.42e-13; heterozygote OR 1.26, homozygote OR 1.58); GWAS Catalog GCST000017 records rs6983267-G.

entries.label: Stacey et al., Nat Genet 2007
entries.fetchedTitle: Common variants on chromosomes 2q35 and 16q12 confer susceptibility to estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer.
entries.note: About 25% of European-descent people are homozygous for rs13387042 allele A on 2q35 with an estimated 1.44-fold risk; risk confined to estrogen receptor-positive tumours; no genes identified in the block.

entries.label: Whibley et al., Nat Rev Cancer 2009
entries.fetchedTitle: p53 polymorphisms: cancer implications.
entries.note: Review abstract says only a small fraction, if any, of TP53 SNPs are expected to perturb p53 function measurably. It does not mention codon 72 or its population frequencies; full text not retrievable.

entries.label: Raimondi et al., Int J Cancer 2008
entries.fetchedTitle: MC1R variants, melanoma and red hair color phenotype: a meta-analysis.
entries.note: Meta-analysis: p.R151C significantly associated with melanoma and strongly with red hair (OR 8.10); some MC1R variants act via non-pigmentary pathways.

entries.label: Hung et al., Nature 2008
entries.fetchedTitle: A susceptibility locus for lung cancer maps to nicotinic acetylcholine receptor subunit genes on 15q25.
entries.note: Abstract supports a 15q25 locus (CHRNA5, CHRNA3, CHRNB4) strongly associated with lung cancer. It does not name rs1051730; GWAS Catalog GCST000170 records rs8034191-C for this paper.

entries.label: Keskitalo et al., Hum Mol Genet 2009
entries.fetchedTitle: Association of serum cotinine level with a cluster of three nicotinic acetylcholine receptor genes (CHRNA3/CHRNA5/CHRNB4) on chromosome 15.
entries.note: Abstract: rs1051730 showed the strongest association with serum cotinine and cigarettes per day in 516 daily smokers. It does not say which allele raises cotinine, and no cited source confirms the report's A-allele lung-cancer statement.

entries.label: Eeles et al., Nat Genet 2008
entries.fetchedTitle: Multiple newly identified loci associated with prostate cancer susceptibility.
entries.note: GWAS identified MSMB among seven new prostate cancer loci; GWAS Catalog GCST000152 records rs10993994-T (OR 1.25). Ensembl places rs10993994 at GRCh37 10:51549496 T/C and GRCh38 10:46046326 A/G, so the reported T is the report's GRCh38 A.
entries.contentNote: Lower PSP94 levels in AA are not in this source.

entries.label: Broderick et al., Nat Genet 2007
entries.fetchedTitle: A genome-wide association study shows that common alleles of SMAD7 influence colorectal cancer risk.
entries.note: rs4939827 in SMAD7 associated with colorectal cancer (P-trend 1.0e-12); GWAS Catalog GCST000113 records rs4939827-T (OR 1.16).

entries.label: Landi et al., Am J Hum Genet 2009
entries.fetchedTitle: A genome-wide association study of lung cancer identifies a region of chromosome 5p15 associated with risk for adenocarcinoma.
entries.note: rs2736100 (TERT) associated with lung adenocarcinoma (meta OR 1.24) but not squamous or small cell; GWAS Catalog GCST000506 records rs2736100-G, the report's forward-strand C (non-palindromic C/A vs G/T).
entries.contentNote: 'The link also appears in people who never smoked' is not in this abstract.

entries.label: McKay et al., Nat Genet 2008
entries.fetchedTitle: Lung cancer susceptibility locus at 5p15.33.
entries.note: Two independent 5p15.33 markers (rs402710, rs2736100) associated with lung cancer and replicated; the region contains TERT and CLPTM1L. Supports 'common variation near TERT is linked to' lung cancer.

entries.label: Shete et al., Nat Genet 2009
entries.fetchedTitle: Genome-wide association study identifies five susceptibility loci for glioma.
entries.note: Glioma GWAS: rs2736100 (TERT) OR 1.27, P = 1.50e-17; Table 1 gives G as the risk allele, the report's forward-strand C.

entries.label: Valverde et al., Nature Genetics 1995
entries.fetchedTitle: Variants of the melanocyte-stimulating hormone receptor gene are associated with red hair and fair skin in humans.
entries.note: Abstract supports MC1R regulating the phaeomelanin/eumelanin balance and MC1R variants in over 80% of people with red hair or poorly tanning fair skin. It does not name R151C or R160W, and neither citation on this report confirms those two variants, so the report's central claim has no confirming source.

entries.label: Hernando et al., Photodermatology Photoimmunology & Photomedicine 2018
entries.fetchedTitle: Genetic variants associated with skin photosensitivity in a southern European population from Spain.
entries.note: Abstract: MC1R R alleles (as a class) associated with sunlight sensitivity in 456 Spaniards. Which variants were counted as R alleles is not in the abstract; full text not retrievable.

entries.label: Han et al., PLoS Genetics 2008
entries.fetchedTitle: A genome-wide association study identifies novel alleles associated with hair color and skin pigmentation.
entries.note: IRF4 rs12203592 associated with hair colour (P = 7.46e-127), skin colour, eye colour and tanning ability (P = 3.9e-89); the variant allele T (WT/VT C/T, MAF 0.17) was associated with lighter skin, less tanning ability and light eye colour.
entries.contentNote: More freckling is not in this source.

entries.label: Hernando et al., Photodermatology Photoimmunology & Photomedicine 2018
entries.fetchedTitle: Genetic variants associated with skin photosensitivity in a southern European population from Spain.
entries.note: IRF4 rs12203592 significantly associated with sunlight sensitivity in a Spanish sample (Bonferroni level); supports the report's statement that it is a strong signal for how skin responds to sunlight. Direction comes from Han et al. 2008.

entries.label: Eriksson et al., PLoS Genetics 2010
entries.fetchedTitle: Web-based, participant-driven studies yield novel genetic associations for common traits.
entries.note: rs10427255 near ZEB2 associated with photic sneeze reflex (OR 1.32); Table 10: 40.1% of CC, 32.1% of TC and 27.6% of TT reported sneezing, so C is linked to more reports.

entries.label: Wang et al., Scientific Reports 2019
entries.fetchedTitle: A genome-wide association study on photic sneeze reflex in the Chinese population.
entries.note: Wang 2019 states that each copy of the minor allele T (Chinese sample, T frequency 0.44) conferred 68% higher odds of the reflex.
entries.defect: The report says 'Studies in both European-ancestry and Chinese groups link the C allele to a higher chance of the reflex' and 'Both cited studies linked C, rather than T'. The Chinese study reports T as the risk allele. The report's statement about this source is contradicted by it.

entries.label: MacIntyre et al., Environmental Health Perspectives 2014
entries.fetchedTitle: GSTP1 and TNF Gene variants and associations between air pollution and incident childhood asthma: the traffic, asthma and genetics (TAG) study.
entries.note: Pooled six birth cohorts (5,115 children): for GSTP1 rs1695 (A>G, Ile105Val) minor-allele carriers, NO2 was associated with current and ever asthma (OR 1.43, 1.36) versus 0.82 and 1.12 in major homozygotes; interaction not significant after correction (0.48, 0.09).

entries.label: Davies et al., Nature Genetics 1996
entries.fetchedTitle: The effect of the human serum paraoxonase polymorphism is reversed with diazoxon, soman and sarin.
entries.note: Arg192 PON1 hydrolyses paraoxon rapidly and Gln192 slowly; the effect is reversed for diazoxon, soman and especially sarin; individuals express widely different PON1 levels.

entries.label: Key et al., PLoS Genetics 2018
entries.fetchedTitle: Human local adaptation of the TRPM8 cold receptor along a latitudinal cline.
entries.note: Upstream TRPM8 variant rs10166942: frequency from 5% (Nigeria) to 88% (Finland), following latitude; the derived allele (T, 0.83 in Europe) was raised by positive selection; the ancestral allele is protective of migraine.

entries.label: Gavva et al., Scientific Reports 2019
entries.fetchedTitle: Reduced TRPM8 expression underpins reduced migraine risk and attenuated cold pain sensation in humans.
entries.note: TRPM8 expression is lower from the rs10166942[C] chromosome in human dorsal root ganglia; C carriers needed lower temperatures and longer exposure to reach the cold pain threshold; C is the reduced-migraine-risk allele.

entries.label: Chasman et al., Nature Genetics 2011
entries.fetchedTitle: Genome-wide association study reveals three susceptibility loci for common migraine in the general population.
entries.note: Population-based migraine GWAS: rs10166942 (TRPM8) OR 0.85, P = 5.5e-12; GWAS Catalog GCST001105 records rs10166942-T as the risk allele (OR 1.18, frequency 0.81).

entries.label: Hromatka et al., Human Molecular Genetics 2015
entries.fetchedTitle: Genetic variants associated with motion sickness point to roles for inner ear development, neurological processes and glucose homeostasis.
entries.note: Supports the 80,494-person 23andMe car-sickness GWAS, 35 genome-wide SNPs, one in three highly susceptible, sex-specific effects up to three times stronger in women, and rs2153535 G raising susceptibility (effect +0.046 per G). Table 2 reports rs66800491 alleles A/G with effect -0.078 per copy of the second allele (G, frequency 0.683) on a scale of increasing motion sickness.
entries.defect: rs66800491 direction appears reversed: the source's Table 2 gives each G copy a lower motion-sickness score (effect -0.078), while the report says G is linked to more car sickness and AA to less. The band is also given as 3q13.2 in the report and 3q13.13 in the source.

entries.label: Friedman et al., Human Molecular Genetics 2009
entries.fetchedTitle: GRM7 variants confer susceptibility to age-related hearing impairment.
entries.scope: abstract (+ Luo 2013 full text for SNP identity)
entries.note: First whole-genome association study for age-related hearing impairment identified a replicated SNP in GRM7; mGluR7 is expressed in inner-ear hair cells. Luo et al. 2013 identifies Friedman's top-ranked SNP as rs11928865.
entries.contentNote: The Taiwanese study with no allelic association is not among the report's citations.

entries.label: Luo et al., PLoS One 2013
entries.fetchedTitle: Association of GRM7 variants with different phenotype patterns of age-related hearing impairment in an elderly male Han Chinese population.
entries.note: In 982 Han Chinese men with ARHI and 324 controls, rs11928865 (A>T) associated with ARHI (OR 1.599); TT more frequent in the sloping and 2-4 kHz loss subgroups.

entries.label: Wang et al., The Lancet 2010
entries.fetchedTitle: Common genetic determinants of vitamin D insufficiency: a genome-wide association study.
entries.note: rs2282679 in GC is the strongest 25-hydroxyvitamin D signal (P = 1.9e-109) in 33,996 Europeans; Table 2 shows minor homozygotes with the lowest mean 25-OH D and Table 3 an OR of 1.63 for insufficiency per risk allele. Ensembl gives G as the minor allele (1000 Genomes EUR 0.247), so GG is the lowest group.

entries.label: Hinds et al., Nature Genetics 2013
entries.fetchedTitle: A genome-wide association meta-analysis of self-reported allergy identifies shared and allergy-specific susceptibility loci.
entries.note: Self-reported allergy GWAS meta-analysis of 53,862 people; IL13 had nominal support; GWAS Catalog GCST002083 records rs20541-A with increased self-reported allergy (P = 1e-6).
entries.contentNote: The higher blood IgE statement is not in this source and no other citation on the report carries it.

entries.label: Edenberg, Alcohol Res Health 2007
entries.fetchedTitle: The genetics of alcohol metabolism: role of alcohol dehydrogenase and aldehyde dehydrogenase variants.
entries.note: Review: certain ADH1B alleles encode more active enzymes giving faster ethanol-to-acetaldehyde conversion with a protective effect on alcoholism risk; ADH1B*1 (Arg48) is the reference allele. Supports the fast His48/*2 protective statement.

entries.label: Feder et al., Nat Genet 1996
entries.fetchedTitle: A novel MHC class I-like gene is mutated in patients with hereditary haemochromatosis.
entries.note: Identified the HFE (HLA-H) gene mutated in hereditary haemochromatosis; a missense change found homozygous in 83% of 178 patients; carrier frequency about 1 in 10 of Northern European descent.

entries.label: Allen et al., N Engl J Med 2008
entries.fetchedTitle: Iron-overload-related disease in HFE hereditary hemochromatosis.
entries.note: Melbourne cohort: iron-overload-related disease in 28.4% of male and 1.2% of female C282Y homozygotes; matches the report's ~28% men and ~1% women figures.

entries.label: Feder et al., Nat Genet 1996
entries.fetchedTitle: A novel MHC class I-like gene is mutated in patients with hereditary haemochromatosis.
entries.note: Establishes HFE as the haemochromatosis gene with two missense alterations (C282Y and H63D). Supports H63D being one of the HFE variants; H63D-specific severity is measured by the report and not overclaimed to this source.

entries.label: Allen et al., N Engl J Med 2008
entries.fetchedTitle: Iron-overload-related disease in HFE hereditary hemochromatosis.
entries.note: Only one non-C282Y-homozygote (a compound heterozygote) had documented iron-overload disease; supports the report's statement that H63D rarely causes overload on its own and matters mainly with C282Y.

entries.label: Bosma et al., N Engl J Med 1995
entries.fetchedTitle: The genetic basis of the reduced expression of bilirubin UDP-glucuronosyltransferase 1 in Gilbert's syndrome.
entries.note: Gilbert's syndrome is due to a longer A(TA)7TAA promoter (UGT1A1*28) reducing enzyme expression; homozygotes had higher serum bilirubin. Supports the *28 promoter and reduced-activity mechanism the report ties to rs887829.

entries.label: Johnson et al., Hum Mol Genet 2009
entries.fetchedTitle: Genome-wide association meta-analysis for total serum bilirubin levels.
entries.note: Bilirubin GWAS meta-analysis: UGT1A1 is the strongest locus (explains ~18% of variation) and SLCO1B1 rs4149056 reduces a hepatic transporter's activity, with drug-metabolism relevance; supports the report's UGT1A1 and irinotecan/SLCO1B1 points. GWAS Catalog GCST000386 curates the UGT1A1 tag rs6742078 (LD partner of rs887829), not rs887829 by name.

entries.label: Kim et al., Science 2003
entries.fetchedTitle: Positional cloning of the human quantitative trait locus underlying taste sensitivity to phenylthiocarbamide.
entries.note: Positional cloning: three coding SNPs give five TAS2R38 haplotypes that explain the bimodal PTC sensitivity and 55-85% of its variance; specific haplotypes carry distinct phenotypes. Supports the Ala49Pro (PAV/AVI) taster mechanism.

entries.label: Monsuur et al., PLoS One 2008
entries.fetchedTitle: Effective detection of human leukocyte antigen risk alleles in celiac disease using tag single nucleotide polymorphisms.
entries.note: rs2187668 tags DQ2.5 (positive allele T, CEU 0.09) with sensitivity 1.000 and specificity 0.999; six tag SNPs predict the HLA risk types of over 95% of celiac patients.

entries.label: Lindesmith et al., Nat Med 2003
entries.fetchedTitle: Human susceptibility and resistance to Norwalk virus infection.
entries.note: Human challenge model: 29% were homozygous recessive for FUT2 and did not express the H type-1 ligand; the FUT2 susceptibility (non-secretor) allele was fully penetrant against Norwalk infection at any dose. Supports the non-secretor resistance statement.

entries.label: Romeo et al., Nat Genet 2008
entries.fetchedTitle: Genetic variation in PNPLA3 confers susceptibility to nonalcoholic fatty liver disease.
entries.note: rs738409[G] (I148M) strongly associated with hepatic fat (P = 5.9e-10) and inflammation; most common in Hispanics; hepatic fat more than twofold higher in GG than noncarriers. Matches the report's G/Met148 direction and 'about twice as much' figure.

entries.label: McPherson et al., Science 2007
entries.fetchedTitle: A common allele on chromosome 9 associated with coronary heart disease.
entries.note: GWAS: a 58-kb 9p21 interval near CDKN2A/CDKN2B consistently associated with coronary heart disease in >23,000 people across four Caucasian populations, containing no annotated genes. Supports the report's 9p21 CAD locus statement.

entries.label: Clarke et al., N Engl J Med 2009
entries.fetchedTitle: Genetic variants associated with Lp(a) lipoprotein level and coronary disease.
entries.note: Abstract names rs10455872 and reports LPA variants associated with Lp(a) level and coronary disease. Supports the report's rs10455872 Lp(a) and coronary-disease statement.

entries.label: Musunuru et al., Nature 2010
entries.fetchedTitle: From noncoding variant to phenotype via SORT1 at the 1p13 cholesterol locus.
entries.note: Full text names rs599839; the paper shows the 1p13 SORT1 locus (via rs12740374 creating a C/EBP site) drives LDL-C and MI. Supports the report's SORT1/LDL mechanism.

entries.label: Willer et al., Nat Genet 2008
entries.fetchedTitle: Newly identified loci that influence lipid concentrations and risk of coronary artery disease.
entries.note: Lipid GWAS; GWAS Catalog GCST000132 records rs599839-A increasing LDL by 5.48 mg/dl (P = 6e-33), matching the report's 'each A copy ... LDL a few mg/dL higher'.

entries.label: Willer et al., Nat Genet 2008
entries.fetchedTitle: Newly identified loci that influence lipid concentrations and risk of coronary artery disease.
entries.note: GWAS Catalog GCST000132 records rs6511720-G raising LDL by 9.17 mg/dl (freq 0.90), so the minor T allele lowers LDL, matching the report's 'T ... LDL about 6 to 7 mg/dL lower per copy' direction.

entries.label: Jeunemaitre et al., Cell 1992
entries.fetchedTitle: Molecular basis of human hypertension: role of angiotensinogen.
entries.note: Found genetic linkage between AGT and hypertension and association of AGT molecular variants (M235T) with the disease and with higher plasma angiotensinogen. Supports the report's AGT/angiotensinogen/blood-pressure statement (rs699 = M235T, not named in this 1992 paper).

entries.label: Poort et al., Blood 1996
entries.fetchedTitle: A common genetic variation in the 3'-untranslated region of the prothrombin gene is associated with elevated plasma prothrombin levels and an increase in venous thrombosis.
entries.note: The 3'-UTR prothrombin G20210A variant is associated with elevated plasma prothrombin and increased venous thrombosis; about 2% carrier prevalence. Matches the report.

entries.label: Frosst et al., Nat Genet 1995
entries.fetchedTitle: A candidate genetic risk factor for vascular disease: a common mutation in methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase.
entries.note: MTHFR C677T produces a thermolabile enzyme with reduced activity; hyperhomocysteinaemia is a vascular-disease risk factor. Supports the report's C677T / reduced-activity / homocysteine statement.

entries.label: Gudbjartsson et al., Nature 2007
entries.fetchedTitle: Variants conferring risk of atrial fibrillation on chromosome 4q25.
entries.note: 4q25 variants confer atrial fibrillation risk; GWAS Catalog GCST000051 records rs2200733-T (OR 1.72), matching the report's 'each T copy ... moderate shift'.

entries.label: Thompson et al., JAMA 2008
entries.fetchedTitle: Association of cholesteryl ester transfer protein genotypes with CETP mass and activity, lipid levels, and coronary risk.
entries.note: Abstract names rs708272 (TaqIB) and assesses CETP genotypes against CETP mass/activity, lipids and coronary risk. Supports the report's CETP/HDL/coronary statement.

entries.label: Yang et al., Am J Hum Genet 2003
entries.fetchedTitle: ACTN3 genotype is associated with human elite athletic performance.
entries.note: ACTN3 R577X homozygosity leaves alpha-actinin-3 absent in 18% of healthy white people; elite sprint athletes have higher 577R frequencies and there is a sprint/endurance trade-off. Supports the report's endurance/sprint pattern.

entries.label: Tharabenjasin et al., PLoS One 2019
entries.fetchedTitle: Association of PPARGC1A Gly428Ser (rs8192678) polymorphism with potential for athletic ability and sports performance: A meta-analysis.
entries.note: Meta-analysis of PPARGC1A rs8192678 (Gly482Ser) and athletic ability/sports performance; full text names rs8192678. Supports the weak/mixed association the report describes. The paper's title mis-numbers the change as Gly428Ser; the report's Gly482Ser is correct.

entries.label: Wang et al., Lancet 2010
entries.fetchedTitle: Common genetic determinants of vitamin D insufficiency: a genome-wide association study.
entries.note: rs10741657 near CYP2R1 associated with 25-OH-D (P = 3.3e-20). Table 2: minor homozygotes had higher 25-OH-D; Ensembl gives minor allele A, so A higher and G lower, matching the report.

entries.label: Hazra et al., Nat Genet 2008
entries.fetchedTitle: Common variants of FUT2 are associated with plasma vitamin B12 levels.
entries.note: rs602662 in FUT2 associated with plasma B12 (P = 3.51e-15), in strong LD with the W143X nonsecretor variant. Table 1: Ser/Ser (A allele) geometric mean 489.82 vs Gly/Gly (G) 417.05, so A (reduced-function/nonsecretor) tracks higher B12 and G (secretor) lower, matching the report.

entries.label: Tanaka et al., PLoS Genet 2009
entries.fetchedTitle: Genome-wide association study of plasma polyunsaturated fatty acids in the InCHIANTI Study.
entries.note: rs174537 (FADS1) associated with plasma PUFAs. Table 2: G/G has the lowest linoleic acid (substrate) and highest conversion products, so G tracks better conversion and T lower, matching the report.

entries.label: Benyamin et al., Nat Genet 2009
entries.fetchedTitle: Common variants in TMPRSS6 are associated with iron status and erythrocyte volume.
entries.note: rs855791 (TMPRSS6 V736A) associated with serum iron, transferrin saturation and MCV; the valine/low-iron allele (the paper's T) decreases iron and haemoglobin, matching the report's 'valine form tracks slightly lower iron and haemoglobin'. Strand letter differs (report A = paper T for the valine allele).

entries.label: Allebrandt et al., Mol Psychiatry 2013
entries.fetchedTitle: A K(ATP) channel gene effect on sleep duration: from genome-wide association studies to function in Drosophila.
entries.note: rs11046205 (ABCC9, a KATP-channel gene) associated with sleep duration in European samples, with a Drosophila functional follow-up. Supports the report's discovery statement.

entries.label: Jones et al., PLoS Genet 2016
entries.fetchedTitle: Genome-Wide Association Analyses in 128,266 Individuals Identifies New Morningness and Sleep Duration Loci.
entries.note: UK Biobank GWAS of sleep duration in 128,266 people; full text names rs11046205. Supports the report's 'much larger study' counter-evidence framing.

entries.label: Hu et al., Nat Commun 2016
entries.fetchedTitle: GWAS of 89,283 individuals identifies genetic variants associated with self-reporting of being a morning person.
entries.note: 23andMe GWAS of 89,283 people for self-reported morningness; RGS16 is close to the top hit and RGS16-knockout mice have a longer circadian period. Supports the report's RGS16 morning-person statement. The exact tag rs516134 is not named in the parts retrieved; the RGS16 locus and study size match exactly.

entries.label: Timpson et al., Am J Clin Nutr 2010
entries.fetchedTitle: Genetic variation at the SLC23A1 locus is associated with circulating concentrations of L-ascorbic acid (vitamin C): evidence from 5 independent studies with >15,000 participants.
entries.note: rs33972313 at SLC23A1 associated with circulating L-ascorbic acid across five studies (>15,000 people); abstract and full text name the SNP. Supports the report's ~6 umol/L-per-T-copy statement.

entries.label: Willcox et al., Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 2008
entries.fetchedTitle: FOXO3A genotype is strongly associated with human longevity.
entries.note: FOXO3A strongly associated with human longevity via the insulin/IGF-1 pathway in long-lived men of Japanese ancestry. Supports the report's FOXO3 longevity statement (rs2802292 is one of the three reported SNPs, not named in the abstract).

entries.label: Flachsbart et al., Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 2009
entries.fetchedTitle: Association of FOXO3A variation with human longevity confirmed in German centenarians.
entries.note: Confirms FOXO3A longevity association in German centenarians, replicating Willcox 2008's three SNPs. Supports the report's cross-cohort replication statement.

entries.label: Schächter et al., Nat Genet 1994
entries.fetchedTitle: Genetic associations with human longevity at the APOE and ACE loci.
entries.note: Centenarian case-control study: the APOE epsilon-4 allele is under-represented in centenarians. Supports the report's e4-less-common-at-100 statement.

entries.label: Deelen et al., Nat Commun 2019
entries.fetchedTitle: A meta-analysis of genome-wide association studies identifies multiple longevity genes.
entries.note: Longevity GWA meta-analysis; abstract and full text name rs429358 and rs7412 (the APOE e-defining SNPs). Supports the report's e2/e4 longevity statement.

entries.label: Barzilai et al., JAMA 2003
entries.fetchedTitle: Unique lipoprotein phenotype and genotype associated with exceptional longevity.
entries.note: Ashkenazi longevity study: CETP valine (I405V) genotype associated with exceptional longevity, larger HDL/LDL particles and lower CETP. Supports the report (rs5882 = I405V, not named in the abstract).

entries.label: Bonafè et al., J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2003
entries.fetchedTitle: Polymorphic variants of insulin-like growth factor I (IGF-I) receptor and phosphoinositide 3-kinase genes affect IGF-I plasma levels and human longevity: cues for an evolutionarily conserved mechanism of life span control.
entries.note: IGF-IR (codon 1013 G/A = rs2229765) and PI3K variants affect IGF-I plasma levels and human longevity; the A/low-IGF-1 allele more frequent in long-lived people. Matches the report.

entries.label: Kilic et al., PLoS One 2015
entries.fetchedTitle: A remarkable age-related increase in SIRT1 protein expression against oxidative stress in elderly: SIRT1 gene variants and longevity in human.
entries.note: Small Turkish study of SIRT1 rs7895833 A>G and SIRT1 protein levels in the elderly; abstract and full text name the SNP. Supports the report's tentative single-study framing.

entries.label: Codd et al., Nat Genet 2013
entries.fetchedTitle: Identification of seven loci affecting mean telomere length and their association with disease.
entries.note: Telomere-length GWAS. Table 1: rs2736100 effect allele A shortens telomeres (beta -0.078), so the other allele C lengthens, matching the report's 'C copy ... slightly longer telomeres'.

entries.label: Codd et al., Nat Genet 2013
entries.fetchedTitle: Identification of seven loci affecting mean telomere length and their association with disease.
entries.note: Table 1: rs10936599 effect allele T shortens telomeres (beta -0.097), so C lengthens, matching the report's 'C ... longer, T ... shorter'.

entries.label: Arking et al., Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 2002
entries.fetchedTitle: Association of human aging with a functional variant of klotho.
entries.note: First KLOTHO functional-variant human survival study (KL-VS); supports the report's klotho/aging statement (rs9536314 = F352V of the KL-VS haplotype, not named in this 2002 microsatellite-marker paper).

entries.label: Dubal et al., Cell Rep 2014
entries.fetchedTitle: Life extension factor klotho enhances cognition.
entries.note: KL-VS heterozygosity associated with enhanced cognition and higher serum klotho; homozygotes excluded. Supports the report's heterozygote-advantage pattern.

entries.label: Ørsted et al., J Exp Med 2007
entries.fetchedTitle: Tumor suppressor p53 Arg72Pro polymorphism and longevity, cancer survival, and risk of cancer in the general population.
entries.note: Danish general-population study (9,219 people) of TP53 Arg72Pro and longevity/cancer survival. Supports the report (rs1042522 = Arg72Pro; the report's 9,219 figure matches).

entries.label: van Heemst et al., Exp Gerontol 2005
entries.fetchedTitle: Variation in the human TP53 gene affects old age survival and cancer mortality.
entries.note: Review/meta-analysis: TP53 variation affects old-age survival and cancer mortality, framed as a tumour-suppression versus tissue-renewal balance. Supports the report's mechanism statement.

entries.label: Christiansen et al., Mech Ageing Dev 2004
entries.fetchedTitle: Modest implication of interleukin-6 promoter polymorphisms in longevity.
entries.note: IL-6 promoter polymorphism modestly implicated in longevity; supports the report's cautious -174G/C statement (rs1800795 = -174G/C, not named in the abstract).

entries.label: Binder et al., Nat Genet 2004
entries.fetchedTitle: Polymorphisms in FKBP5 are associated with increased recurrence of depressive episodes and rapid response to antidepressant treatment.
entries.note: FKBP5 SNPs associated with recurrence of depressive episodes and rapid antidepressant response via the HPA axis. Supports the report's FKBP5/stress-response statement (rs1360780 is one of the genotyped SNPs).

entries.label: Klengel et al., Nat Neurosci 2013
entries.fetchedTitle: Allele-specific FKBP5 DNA demethylation mediates gene-childhood trauma interactions.
entries.note: Full text names rs1360780; allele-specific FKBP5 demethylation mediates a gene-by-childhood-trauma interaction. Supports the report's early-life-stress interaction statement.

entries.label: Rodrigues et al., PNAS 2009
entries.fetchedTitle: Oxytocin receptor genetic variation relates to empathy and stress reactivity in humans.
entries.note: rs53576 GG homozygotes showed higher empathy and lower stress reactivity than A carriers. Matches the report.

entries.label: Munafò et al., Biol Psychiatry 2008
entries.fetchedTitle: Association of the dopamine D4 receptor (DRD4) gene and approach-related personality traits: meta-analysis and new data.
entries.note: Meta-analysis of DRD4 VNTR and C-521T (rs1800955) with approach-related traits; evidence uncertain. Supports the report's mixed-evidence C-521T novelty statement.

entries.label: Ferreira et al., Nat Genet 2008
entries.fetchedTitle: Collaborative genome-wide association analysis supports a role for ANK3 and CACNA1C in bipolar disorder.
entries.note: rs1006737 (CACNA1C) supported for bipolar disorder (combined P = 7.0e-8; allele A OR 1.21 in ED-DUB-STEP2). Matches the report's A-allele direction.

entries.label: Ferreira et al., Nat Genet 2008
entries.fetchedTitle: Collaborative genome-wide association analysis supports a role for ANK3 and CACNA1C in bipolar disorder.
entries.note: rs10994336 (ANK3) region of strong association for bipolar disorder (P = 9.1e-9); the minor T allele is the risk allele, matching the report's 'less common T copy ... OR about 1.45'.

entries.label: O'Donovan et al., Nat Genet 2008
entries.fetchedTitle: Identification of loci associated with schizophrenia by genome-wide association and follow-up.
entries.note: GWAS + follow-up gave strongest evidence around ZNF804A (P = 1.61e-7). Supports the report's ZNF804A schizophrenia statement (rs1344706 is the ZNF804A index SNP, not named in the abstract).

entries.label: Howard et al., Nat Neurosci 2019
entries.fetchedTitle: Genome-wide meta-analysis of depression identifies 102 independent variants and highlights the importance of the prefrontal brain regions.
entries.note: Depression GWAS meta-analysis of 807,553 people identifying 102 independent variants. Supports the report's study description (rs12552 near OLFM4 is one of the 102; the exact rsID was not located in the retrieved full text).

entries.label: Brown et al., Mol Psychiatry 2005
entries.fetchedTitle: A regulatory variant of the human tryptophan hydroxylase-2 gene biases amygdala reactivity.
entries.note: A regulatory TPH2 variant biases amygdala reactivity in vivo. Supports the report's -703 G/T amygdala statement (rs4570625 = -703G/T, not named in the abstract).

entries.label: Frayling et al., Science 2007
entries.fetchedTitle: A common variant in the FTO gene is associated with body mass index and predisposes to childhood and adult obesity.
entries.note: A common FTO variant is associated with BMI and predisposes to childhood and adult obesity, with an additive per-allele effect. Supports the report (rs9939609 is the FTO intron-1 variant, not named in the abstract).

entries.label: Loos et al., Nat Genet 2008
entries.fetchedTitle: Common variants near MC4R are associated with fat mass, weight and risk of obesity.
entries.note: rs17782313 188 kb downstream of MC4R was the strongest BMI signal after FTO. Abstract and full text name the SNP; matches the report's MC4R/BMI statement.

entries.label: Altshuler et al., Nat Genet 2000
entries.fetchedTitle: The common PPARgamma Pro12Ala polymorphism is associated with decreased risk of type 2 diabetes.
entries.note: PPARgamma Pro12Ala associated with decreased type 2 diabetes risk (the Ala/G allele protective). Matches the report's C=Pro higher odds, G=Ala lower odds (rs1801282 = Pro12Ala).

entries.label: Gloyn et al., Diabetes 2003
entries.fetchedTitle: Large-scale association studies of variants in genes encoding the pancreatic beta-cell KATP channel subunits Kir6.2 (KCNJ11) and SUR1 (ABCC8) confirm that the KCNJ11 E23K variant is associated with type 2 diabetes.
entries.note: Large-scale study confirming KCNJ11 E23K associated with type 2 diabetes. Supports the report (rs5219 = E23K; lysine/T is the risk allele).

entries.label: Prokopenko et al., Nat Genet 2009
entries.fetchedTitle: Variants in MTNR1B influence fasting glucose levels.
entries.note: MTNR1B variants consistently associated with fasting glucose across ten studies; strongest at rs10830963 (named in abstract and full text). Matches the report's G-allele higher-glucose statement.

entries.label: Rung et al., Nat Genet 2009
entries.fetchedTitle: Genetic variant near IRS1 is associated with type 2 diabetes, insulin resistance and hyperinsulinemia.
entries.note: rs2943641 near IRS1 associated with type 2 diabetes, insulin resistance and hyperinsulinaemia; the C allele carries the risk. Matches the report.

entries.label: Hivert et al., Diabetes 2008
entries.fetchedTitle: Common variants in the adiponectin gene (ADIPOQ) associated with plasma adiponectin levels, type 2 diabetes, and diabetes-related quantitative traits: the Framingham Offspring Study.
entries.note: ADIPOQ common variants (rs17300539 named in abstract and full text) associated with plasma adiponectin; the A allele tracks higher adiponectin. Matches the report.

entries.label: Corella et al., Arch Intern Med 2009
entries.fetchedTitle: APOA2, dietary fat, and body mass index: replication of a gene-diet interaction in 3 independent populations.
